title: ChannelConfig
description: A channel's full config document, stored in channels.config, edited on the Channels screen. Per-video overrides deep-merge at enqueue (chain lists replace wholesale) into the immutable cfg.json snapshot.

production_style.description: D61 - HOW this channel's videos are produced: the durable creative decision a human makes once per channel. It is the channel-side counterpart of a manifest's `category`, and the selection resolver at enqueue turns it into a pipeline name by picking the production-stability manifest of that category. Distinct from `video_type`, which is WHAT the video is (doc, explainer...) and selects a style pack: a faceless doc and a talking-head doc are the same content shape produced two different ways.
production_style.$comment: same enum as pipeline_manifest.category, deliberately - the two must stay comparable

pipeline.description: D60 - pipeline manifest name (contracts/pipelines/<name>.yaml). PINS one exact stage list, overriding production_style: the escape hatch for running a `stability: test` variant of a style. Absent = the resolver picks the manifest matching production_style, and with neither field set, 'faceless'.

checkpoint_policy.description: D62 - HOW FAR the worker runs before asking a human. 'auto' walks the whole manifest straight through (what every video has done until now). 'guided' - shown as REVIEW mode in the UI - stops after every stage the manifest marks `human_approval_on_review_mode` and leaves the video in `awaiting_approval` until someone approves it. Absent = the manifest's own `default_checkpoint_policy`. This is a POLICY ON a pipeline, never a separate pipeline: the same faceless.yaml runs both ways, which is what stops a `faceless-review.yaml` fork existing.
checkpoint_policy.$comment: same enum as pipeline_manifest.default_checkpoint_policy, deliberately - the video-level value overrides the manifest-level one

transcript.description: D63 - what a subtitle CUE is in this channel's subtitles.srt. Read by the transcript stage, which produces the file, and by the beats process, which takes its script breaks from it. Per channel rather than per pipeline: two channels running the same faceless manifest legitimately want different cue sizes, and putting this in the manifest would fork it once per answer.

granularity.description: 'sentence' is what every video has produced until now: the TTS adapter synthesizes one sentence at a time and reports exact per-sentence timings (ai33, flite, mock all do this), so a cue IS a sentence. 'word' emits one cue per word, which is what a beats process that aligns its own script splits needs - it requires ASR (the TTS adapters cannot time inside a sentence), so it re-transcribes the audio. 'segment' keeps whatever chunks the ASR chose, the shape an uploaded subtitles.srt already has.

checkpoint_policy.description: D62 - production MODE. `auto` runs the pipeline straight through (what every video did before this existed). `guided` (shown as 'Review' in the UI) stops after every stage the manifest marks `human_approval_on_review_mode` and waits for a human, so nothing downstream - the render above all - happens on unapproved work. A POLICY on any pipeline, never a separate pipeline: the same manifest runs both ways. Absent = the manifest's `default_checkpoint_policy`, then `auto`.
checkpoint_policy.$comment: the enum matches pipeline_manifest.default_checkpoint_policy so one can fall back to the other

transcript.description: D63 - how finely the transcript stage cuts subtitles.srt. This is what the beat sheet's timing is built from, so it decides where a beat is ALLOWED to start, not just what a caption looks like.

granularity.description: `sentence` (default, and what every video did before this existed): one cue per sentence, timed exactly by the TTS adapter, which synthesises sentence by sentence. `segment`: the ASR's own segmentation, ignoring TTS timings - arbitrary breaks that follow delivery rather than punctuation. `word`: one cue per word, which is what lets a later beats process split the script wherever it likes and still know when each piece is spoken. `segment` and `word` both require local Whisper and cost a transcription pass over audio the TTS already timed.

model.description: provider model id; the agents already read it

prompt.description: prompt pack name (contracts/prompts/script/<name>.json) — layer 2 of the D44 resolution order

research.description: D64 - phase 0 of this agent: one call that gathers what the video is ABOUT before anything writes prose, so the script argues from a brief instead of inventing as it goes. It shares script.llm/model - it is the same bounded agent (D2), not a fourth one, exactly as the spine is a phase of the planner.

enabled.description: false makes the stage write a title-only brief, which is also what a mock provider produces - the script then behaves exactly as it did before research existed

model.description: provider model id; the agents already read it

chunk_target_beats.description: above this many target beats the script is planned in sentence-aligned CHUNKS, one call each, instead of one call for the whole video. A single call handles ~20-30 beats comfortably; past that it truncates or degrades, and one dropped sentence fails full coverage for the entire sheet.

spine.description: phase 1 of this agent on a chunked script: one cheap call that finds where the story TURNS, so sections are cut at joints instead of at even word counts. It shares planner.llm/model — it is the same bounded agent (D2), not a fourth one.

enabled.description: false uses the deterministic word-balanced split, which is also what a failed or malformed spine degrades to

chat.description: editor chat agent (D15); the platform reads it from the video's cfg snapshot

safe_bottom.description: D56 — where captions sit when nothing is in the way: the gap from the bottom edge, as a fraction of frame height. The renderer's resting position.

line_fraction.description: D56 — how tall a caption is, as a fraction of frame height. Used to work out whether a graphic actually lands on it; a caption is not a line, it is a band.

max_lift.description: D56 — how far captions may be raised to clear a graphic. Clearing a full-frame treatment would need more than this (there is no free space under it), and a caption in the middle of the frame is worse than an overlap, so past this limit the caption steps up by one caption height instead.

look.description: The SUBTRACTIVE half of the look. The theme and the style pack say what is AVAILABLE; this says what this channel (or this one video) leaves out, plus the plate that sits behind anything that does not fill the frame. Applied to the embedded theme_doc / style_pack_doc at enqueue, so every stage downstream sees an already-narrowed pack and no agent, compiler or renderer has to know this block exists.

background.description: The plate drawn behind an overlay that does not fill the frame - the D55 fallback card above all. Absent = the flat colour fill both renderers drew before this existed.

image.description: file name in the channel's background library. Rewritten at enqueue to the copy inside the video folder, so the render resolves it like any other asset and a later change to the library never alters a finished video.

exclude.description: Names removed from what the pack offers. Excluding everything a required list holds, or the style pack's default transition, is refused at enqueue rather than silently repaired.

moods.description: moods removed from theme.sound.mood_beds - that span plays with no bed

qa.description: D57 — post-render checks on the finished file, run before a video can reach RENDERED. Every number is a threshold on something ffmpeg measures; loosening one is a channel decision, not a code change.

frame_samples.description: how many frames to look at, spread evenly and inset from both ends (an opening fade is legitimately black)

black_luma_max.description: mean luma at or under which a sampled frame counts as black

max_black_samples.description: how many black samples are tolerated before the video fails — a fade_to_black transition can legitimately land on one

flat_frame_range.description: brightest minus darkest cell of an 8x8 grey sample, at or under which the frame is a flat fill: an overlay covering the shot, or an asset that never decoded. Mean luma alone cannot see this.

silence_dbfs.description: level at or under which audio counts as silence, for both the whole-mix average and the gap check

max_silence_run_s.description: the longest silent stretch allowed inside the mix — a hole in the narration

clip_dbfs.description: peak level at or over which the mix counts as clipping. D49 delivers at -14 LUFS so the platform leaves the mix alone; a clipped peak defeats that.

duration_tolerance_s.description: how far the finished file may differ from the voiceover's own length before it counts as cut short or padded

content_rules.description: channel content rules text, given to the planner

chain.description: order = preference; omission = forbidden; replaced wholesale by overrides

min_score_floor.description: D55 — the score under which a match is not worth showing at all. A source's own min_score decides whether to FALL THROUGH; this decides whether the chain's answer is placed or replaced by a typographic card (style_pack.fallback). 0 = off. Only sources that return a score (the library) are judged.
min_score_floor.$comment: not the same knob as chain[].min_score: that one is per source, this one is the last word

short_clip_fallback.description: D55 — how to cover a slot longer than its footage, first applicable wins. `loop` repeats the source (both renderers), `slow` ramps playback down to at most 0.5x (Remotion only — the ffmpeg profile rejects speed != 1, so it forces the premium route), `freeze` holds the last frame, which is what both renderers did before this existed.

dedup.description: D54 — how hard this channel works to avoid showing the same thing twice in one video. Per-beat resolution is independent by design, which is what lets two adjacent beats about the same subject fetch the same clip.

reuse_window_items.description: how many recent visual items an exact asset id stays blocked for. 0 = the whole video: a segment is spent once. A small number suits a channel with a thin library, where a callback after four minutes reads as a motif rather than as a mistake.

min_hamming_distance.description: near-duplicate threshold on a 64-bit perceptual hash of one frame: a candidate closer than this to a shot already used is skipped. 0 = off (the default, since the check costs one wasted download per repeat); ~6 catches the same footage re-encoded or re-graded, without catching two different shots of the same subject.

sound_pack.description: sound pack name; overrides theme.sound.pack. The pack manifest is embedded as sound_pack_doc at enqueue.

enabled.description: master switch for background music on this channel; false makes the resolve_audio stage a no-op for beds

default_volume.description: D48: a TRIM on the theme's music levels, not the level itself — 1 means 'as the theme mixed it', 0.5 pulls music down 6 dB across the channel. The absolute levels are theme.sound.gain.music_duck / music_lift, so the mix lives in one place.

enabled.description: master switch for sound effects on this channel; overridable per video like any config field

overrides.description: per-video override slot (style pack fields like overlay density ride here in the snapshot)

style_pack_doc.description: full style pack document embedded at enqueue (snapshot, Core Principle 7)

theme_doc.description: full theme document embedded at enqueue (snapshot)

sound_pack_doc.description: full sound pack manifest embedded at enqueue (snapshot). Absent when no pack is resolved, which is how a channel produces silent video.

pipeline_doc.description: full pipeline manifest embedded at enqueue (D60, snapshot). The worker walks THIS list, so editing the manifest never changes an in-flight video and a re-run reproduces the same stage order.

prompts.description: resolved prompt TEXT per role, embedded at enqueue (D44). Editing a prompt afterwards never changes this video; a re-run reproduces the same words.

source.description: which layer of the D44 ladder won

system.description: editable half only; the welded block is appended at call time

media_types.description: INERT for source=library (D76): every library row is an mp4, including one made from an uploaded still, so there is nothing to select between. Still read by other sources.

profile.description: INERT (D76): which library to search. broll-engine binds one profile per API process, so one deployment is one library; kept so the field does not have to be reintroduced when a second one exists.

style.description: ai_image style suffix appended to the visual_intent
